docs.title: Hello!
docs.text:
I am a Ph.D. Candidate in Accounting at IESE Business School. My research examines how firms respond to external stakeholder pressure and how these responses shape corporate disclosure, labor markets, and information environments.

My job market paper, "How Does Public Activism Shape Voluntary Disclosure? Evidence from the Thematic Contents of Conference Calls," studies whether public activism changes the thematic content of managerial communication in earnings conference calls. Using textual analysis, I focus on how stakeholder salience, public scrutiny, and managers' attention to non-financial issues shape voluntary disclosure.

More broadly, my work studies corporate disclosure, stakeholder pressure, public activism, textual analysis, capital markets, labor markets, and sustainability/green finance.

I am especially interested in settings where public information, social pressure, and firm communication intersect.

docs.title: How Does Public Activism Shape Voluntary Disclosure? Evidence from the Thematic Contents of Conference Calls
docs.text:
Authorship: Single-authored

Draft Slides Abstract

Abstract

This paper examines how public activism shapes firms' voluntary disclosure choices in conference calls. Using textual analysis of earnings call transcripts, I study whether local public activism changes the thematic content of managerial communication, with a focus on stakeholder salience, public scrutiny, and managers' attention to non-financial issues.

Award: The Sue Hrasky Best PhD Paper Prize

Selected presentations: Financial Reporting and Business Communication Conference; Journal of International Accounting Research Conference; European Accounting Association Doctoral Colloquium; British Accounting and Finance Association Annual Conference.

docs.title: Do NGO Campaigns Affect Firms' Labor Markets? Evidence from Employee Reviews, Job Postings, and Worker Flows
docs.text:
Coauthor: Igor Kadach

Abstract

This paper examines whether NGO activism affects firms through the labor market. Combining NGO campaign data with employee reviews, job postings, and worker-flow outcomes, the paper studies how external stakeholder pressure shapes employees' perceptions, firms' labor demand, and worker mobility.

docs.title: Mapping Digital Opacity: Corporate Restrictions on Automated Web Access
docs.text:
Coauthors: Long Cheng and Igor Kadach

Abstract

This paper uses a unique dataset of U.S. firms from 2001 to 2025 to revisit the classic trade-off between information benefits and proprietary costs in the digital era. We examine how firms restrict automated web access and study what these restrictions reveal about corporate transparency, information access, and strategic disclosure choices.

docs.title: Green Banks and the Demand for Green Skills: Evidence from Job Postings
docs.text:
Coauthors: Claudio Rizzi, Simon Xu, and Paul Yoo

Abstract

This paper examines the labor-market consequences of green banks in the United States. Using job-posting data, we study whether green finance initiatives affect firms' labor demand, with a focus on employment decisions, workforce composition, and the demand for green skills.
